subject: Evening surge: SSE/WebSocket throughput errors and p99 regression - OmniCommerce escalation
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@omnicommerce.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: OmniCommerce Support <support@omnicommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 19:12:03 -0700
Subject: high chat errors during evening surge - urgent

Marcus —

We started to see elevated errors and disconnects on your streaming chat endpoint (SSE) around 18:45 PST during our evening traffic spike. Users experienced broken sessions and some messages failed to deliver. p95 latency was fine but p99 rose sharply and we saw a 7% increase in 500s. This is affecting checkout chat flows for shoppers.

Attached is a sampling of client-side logs and the timestamps where the failures happened. Can you confirm whether this is an issue on your side or something in our connection pattern? We need an ETA for a mitigation; our VP of CX is asking for a timeline.

Thanks,
Jordan
Lead Platform Engineer
OmniCommerce

Jordan — thank you for the heads-up and logs. I’m escalating this immediately to our on-call infra and runtime teams. Initial ask: can you confirm average concurrent connections and the typical message size during the spike window? That will help narrow whether this is batching/cache or connection throttling.

Immediate next steps from our side: 1) We’ll pull host-level SSE metrics and per-model tail-latency traces for 18:30–19:00 PST. 2) Ops will check for autoscaler oscillation or node OOMs. 3) If we confirm degraded throughput due to batching/queue backlog we’ll flip a conservative routing policy to lower-latency nodes and enable a short-lived cache bypass for OmniCommerce while we stabilize.

I’m looping in Evelyn, Laura, and Rishi for visibility — will update in ~25 minutes with findings.

— Marcus

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 19:45:22 -07:00
Subject: internal: initial ops findings for OmniCommerce SSE spike

Folks — quick ops summary from the 18:30–19:00 window.

What we observed:
- P95 remained ~120ms but p99 jumped from baseline ~420ms to ~1.8s for SSE publish events.
- Several adapter nodes reported short-lived FD exhaustion and ephemeral connection resets; not a total cluster OOM.
- Autoscaler added nodes but scale-up lag and warmup plus KV cache thrashing produced a brief backlog on the distributor layer.
- Error rate for 5xx rose to ~6.9% for OmniCommerce routing policy; other tenants on the same capacity pool saw <1% impact.

Immediate mitigations applied (19:00):
- Warmed and promoted a dedicated small pool for OmniCommerce traffic, routing ~30% of traffic to cold nodes for faster connection handoff.
- Increased file-descriptor ulimit on adapters to reduce resets.
- Temporarily increased request concurrency limit on the tenant route and disabled prefix-KV eviction for 10 minutes.

Customer impact: likely reduced after 19:05 but we need to monitor another 2+ peak windows to validate. Laura to coordinate with CS for a customer-safe explanation.

Evelyn
Director, Runtime Reliability

Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 21:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: high chat errors during evening surge - urgent

Jordan — thanks again for the detailed logs and patience. Short update and next steps: 

Summary of cause: our runtime saw transient connection-resource exhaustion on a shared adapter pool during OmniCommerce’s evening concurrency spike. That interacted with our autoscaler warmup behavior and cache eviction pattern, producing a temporary p99 latency regression and increased 5xx rate for the tenant route.

What we did:
- Promoted a hot pool and adjusted routing to reduce multi-tenant sharing for the next 48 hours.
- Increased adapter FD limits and adjusted autoscaler cooldowns to avoid oscillation during sudden surges.
- Disabled aggressive KV eviction for pinned prefixes for 30 minutes to reduce cache churn while we validated stability.

Customer-facing mitigation: we will keep OmniCommerce routed to a warmed pool for the next 24 hours and run a targeted load test with them tomorrow at 18:30 PST to validate. We’ve prepared a post-incident summary and a small goodwill credit for the impacted window.

Requested customer asks: can you confirm whether the load pattern tomorrow will be similar to tonight (concurrent connections and average message size)? Laura, can you schedule the joint load test and coordinate the credit/email to Jordan’s procurement contact? Rishi, please file RED-4092 with the follow-up action items for infra changes and a small regression test to prevent recurrence.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a full RCA and timeline.

— Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
